findings.text: The extractor stores `deriving instance BEq for A, /-` for the valid command `deriving instance BEq for A, /- second type -/ B`, so every generated instance gets the wrong text hash. Fix: Use Lean’s parsed command boundaries and add a regression test that checks the stored text through `B`.

A line containing `deriving instance` inside a block comment can start a match that extends through a later command’s `for`, causing an ordinary instance between them to receive the comment and both declarations as its source. Fix: Match only actual deriving commands and test that an intervening ordinary instance retains its own text.

The cache test passes if the version bump is reverted because `"an older extractor"` differs from both production version strings. Fix: Populate the store under `lean-code-store-prototype-1`, restore the production version, and require all five modules to be extracted again.

The status says extraction ends at the last type, but the extractor stops inside a valid quoted target such as `«A B»`. Fix: Qualify the status entry to describe the multiline cases the regression test verifies.
